root_cause.text: The loop condition in imx8m_blk_ctrl_remove() was missing the loop variable increment check, causing an infinite loop that accesses bc->domains array elements beyond the valid range.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `for (i = 0; bc->onecell_data.num_domains; i++)` to `for (i = 0; i < bc->onecell_data.num_domains; i++)`. The original condition `bc->onecell_data.num_domains` is a non-zero constant that never changes, so the loop never terminates based on the loop variable `i`, resulting in out-of-bounds array access to bc->domains when `i` exceeds the valid index range.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix infinite loop condition in imx8m_blk_ctrl_remove by adding missing loop variable comparison to properly iterate through all domains.
intent_record.what: Changed the for loop condition from `i = 0; bc->onecell_data.num_domains; i++` to `i = 0; i < bc->onecell_data.num_domains; i++`. The second clause of the for loop now includes the loop variable `i` in a comparison expression instead of just evaluating the num_domains value.
intent_record.how: The original code had a malformed for loop where the condition clause was missing the loop variable comparison, causing the loop to iterate indefinitely (or not at all, depending on how the compiler interprets the non-zero constant). The corrected code properly compares `i` against `num_domains`, ensuring the loop terminates after iterating through all domains exactly once. This fixes the iteration logic to correctly remove all block control domains during device removal.

candidates.rationale: The loop condition is missing the loop variable comparison. It only checks 'bc->onecell_data.num_domains' (which is always true if non-zero) without comparing 'i' against it. This causes an infinite loop where 'i' keeps incrementing without ever reaching the termination condition, leading to out-of-bounds array access on 'bc->domains[i]'.

vuln_statements.explanation: The loop condition is missing the loop variable comparison against the upper bound. The condition 'bc->onecell_data.num_domains' evaluates to a constant non-zero value (always true), causing the loop to iterate indefinitely without ever terminating. The loop variable 'i' increments without bound, leading to out-of-bounds access of the 'bc->domains[i]' array beyond its valid range of [0, num_domains). The fix requires adding the comparison 'i <' to properly terminate when 'i' reaches 'bc->onecell_data.num_domains'.
